method: give the agent a runnable check; gate the stop deterministically
claim: Claude stops when work looks done; give it a pass/fail check; escalate from in-prompt to /goal evaluator to Stop hook to verification subagent that tries to refute the result
relevance_to_us: Our CI type/function gates are this; a Stop hook running them makes the gate fire inside the agent loop, not only at CI

method: explore -> plan -> implement; interview-then-spec; fresh session to execute spec
claim: Have Claude interview you and write SPEC.md, then start a fresh session to execute it. Best specs name files and interfaces, state out-of-scope, end with an end-to-end verification step
relevance_to_us: Matches our design-doc-first; adds explicit out-of-scope and an end-to-end verification step per spec

method: writer/reviewer split; separate test-writer and implementer
claim: A fresh context improves code review since Claude won't be biased toward code it just wrote. 'have one Claude write tests, then another write code to pass them'
relevance_to_us: Vendor endorses our contract-test/implementer separation (they describe it sequentially; ours is parallel and blind)

method: adversarial review with a scope limit
claim: A reviewer prompted to find gaps will usually report some even when the work is sound; chasing every finding leads to over-engineering: extra abstraction layers, defensive code, tests for impossible cases. Tell the reviewer to flag only correctness/requirement gaps
relevance_to_us: Direct caution for our adversarial design reviewers: constrain them to correctness/contract gaps or they push toward over-abstraction

method: short CLAUDE.md, hooks for must-happen rules
claim: Bloated CLAUDE.md causes Claude to ignore instructions; include architectural decisions specific to the project; use hooks for actions that must happen every time
relevance_to_us: Keep design docs pointed-to rather than resident; enforce the 'what is a system' and small-function rules mechanically

method: simplest pattern that works; evaluator-optimizer; orchestrator-workers
claim: Add complexity only when it demonstrably improves outcomes; evaluator-optimizer fits when there are clear evaluation criteria; human review remains crucial for alignment with broader system requirements
relevance_to_us: Our pipeline is orchestrator-workers + evaluator-optimizer; the bar is that each stage demonstrably earns its cost

method: multi-agent orchestration
claim: Multi-agent beat single-agent by 90.2% on research eval; ~15x chat tokens; 'most coding tasks involve fewer truly parallelizable tasks than research'; domains needing shared context or many inter-agent dependencies are not a good fit today
relevance_to_us: Measured for research, not coding. Supports parallelism only where the interface contract decouples the agents -- which is exactly what our interface-first step buys

method: TDD one test at a time via plan.md; separate structural from behavioral commits
claim: System prompt: Red-Green-Refactor, one test at a time, only enough code to pass, never mix structural and behavioral changes. Warning signs: loops, unrequested functionality, disabling/deleting tests. Still finds 'too much accidental complexity'; takes design control by choosing the next test himself
relevance_to_us: Cheating-by-weakening-tests is the failure our blind contract-test agent prevents; tidy-first commit split is cheap to add as an implementer rule

method: critique of spec-driven dev tools (Kiro, spec-kit, Tessl)
claim: Heavy spec workflows were overkill for small/mid tasks, produced verbose markdown tedious to review; agent frequently did not follow all instructions (regenerated existing classes as duplicates) and also over-applied constitution articles; generation from the same spec was non-deterministic; small iterative steps sit oddly with SDD
relevance_to_us: Specs do not bind the agent by themselves; our design docs only work because CI gates and contract tests enforce them. Keep design docs short and reviewable

method: agent-friendly code shape
claim: Simple code significantly outperforms complex code in agentic contexts; functions over classes, no inheritance/magic, long descriptive names; keep important checks local where the agent will see them; fast, misuse-proof tools; refactor before the codebase sprawls
relevance_to_us: Supports our small-function gate; 'keep checks local' argues against invariants living only in a distant engine-contract doc -- put asserts at the call site too

method: harness engineering; separate planning and execution sessions
claim: When an agent errs, engineer a fix so it never makes that mistake again: AGENTS.md lines each based on a bad behavior, plus scripts so the agent verifies itself. Runs one agent at a time, does not want multiple
relevance_to_us: Route each defect class found in bug hunts into a gate/check, not just a fix

method: treat agent output as semi-black box backed by tests/docs and real use
claim: Admits not reviewing every line; warns of 'normalization of deviance' -- trusting the model at the wrong moment after it has been reliable
relevance_to_us: Argues for keeping independent checks even when the pipeline has been reliable

method: feedback sensors, mutation testing, code-smell-to-refactoring mapping, architecture drift reduction, team of coding agents
claim: Trial: feedback sensors (compilers/linters/tests wired into agent loop as backpressure); mutation testing to expose 'perpetually green' AI-written tests; mapping code smells to refactorings linked to linters. Assess: architecture drift reduction (deterministic analysis + LLM); small role-specific team of agents. Caution: agent instruction bloat, codebase cognitive debt, coding agent swarms, throughput as productivity. Nov 2025: complacency with AI-generated code on Hold; spec-driven dev Assess
relevance_to_us: Mutation testing is the missing check on our contract-test agent; architecture-drift detection is a deterministic complement to the systems inventory

method: measured code-quality trend
claim: 211M changed lines 2020-2024: copy-pasted lines exceeded moved (refactored) lines for the first time in 2024; ~40% fewer moved lines; large rise in duplicated blocks. Secondary reporting, original not read
relevance_to_us: Duplication over reuse is the typical AI design failure; a duplication detector gate targets it. Note: correlational, assistant-era, not agent-era

method: red/green TDD prompt shorthand
claim: Write tests first and watch them fail; skipping the red step risks a test that already passes. 'Use red/green TDD' is enough for capable models
relevance_to_us: Our contract-test agent writes before implementation exists, so tests should be run red against a stub first -- cheap check that each property can fail

method: agents for continuous refactoring; prototype competing options; compound engineering retros
claim: Refactoring is cheap enough for 'zero tolerance' of minor smells via async agent branches; prove technology choices with prototypes; end each project with a retro that updates instructions
relevance_to_us: Cheap parallel prototypes of an interface could replace one designer + review rounds for contested designs

who: Birgitta Boeckeler (Thoughtworks), quoting OpenAI harness engineering post
method: guides (feedforward) + sensors (feedback); computational vs inferential
claim: Computational sensors (types, ArchUnit-style structural tests of module boundaries, dep-cruiser, semgrep) reliably catch duplication, complexity, drift; LLM review catches semantic issues like over-engineering but is costly/probabilistic. Behaviour correctness via AI-generated tests 'puts a lot of faith into the AI-generated tests'. OpenAI enforced a layered architecture with custom linters and structural tests plus recurring 'garbage collection' agents for drift
relevance_to_us: We have type + small-function gates but no structural/dependency test enforcing the systems inventory's boundaries -- the most-cited missing piece. OpenAI primary post 403'd, not read

who: Chen, Sun, Shi, Peng, Gu, Lo, Jiang (arXiv 2026)
method: measured: agent-written tests
claim: On SWE-bench Verified across six LLMs, resolved and unresolved tasks show similar test-writing rates; agent tests are mostly print statements not assertions; prompting more/fewer tests did not significantly change outcomes
relevance_to_us: Agent self-tests written alongside its own code add little; supports separating the test author from the implementer and requiring assertions/properties. Bug-fix setting, not greenfield design

method: measured: test-first reasoning
claim: Writing executable tests before implementation improved results on LiveCodeBench/RepoEval; warns incomplete/incorrect tests give misleading feedback. A secondary summary claimed 'matched failures' (code passes own tests, fails held-out) -- NOT confirmed on the abstract page
relevance_to_us: Weak support for test-first; matched-failure claim unverified

method: Ralph loop: specs folder, one task per fresh-context loop, backpressure
claim: One thing per loop with fresh context; wire in type checker/static analysis as backpressure; 'DO NOT IMPLEMENT PLACEHOLDER'; wrong output means specs are wrong; would not use it in an existing codebase; admits results have gaps
relevance_to_us: Backpressure = our CI gates; placeholder-hunting loops are a cheap later-stage check. Ralph is single-agent and makes no design-quality claim

method: initializer agent writes a JSON feature list (all failing); coding agents do one feature per session and only flip status
claim: Failure modes: one-shotting the whole app; declaring victory early; marking done without end-to-end test. JSON chosen because models overwrite it less than Markdown. Whether specialized testing/QA agents help is 'still unclear' -- untested
relevance_to_us: Our separate contract-test agent is ahead of what Anthropic has tested here; a machine-readable contract/feature list the implementer cannot edit is a cheap guard

method: 16 parallel agents, lock files, no orchestrator; specialized standing roles (dedup agent, Rust design critic, perf, docs); near-perfect test oracle
claim: 'the task verifier is nearly perfect, otherwise Claude will solve the wrong problem'; new features frequently broke existing functionality until CI + stricter enforcement added; code quality 'nowhere near' expert Rust
relevance_to_us: Standing dedup/design-critic agents run over the integrated codebase (not just designs) are a role we lack; regression CI must exist from day one

method: properties extracted from EARS requirements, each traced to a requirement and task; counterexample may indict code, property or spec
claim: Kiro derives property-based tests from spec requirements and checks requirements for contradictions before code; vendor says PBT is evidence not proof
relevance_to_us: Closest published analogue to our contract-test agent; steal: trace each property to a contract clause id, and treat a failing property as possibly a spec bug

method: one-question-at-a-time interview -> spec.md -> reasoning-model plan of small TDD prompts -> execute
claim: Each prompt builds on the last and ends by wiring things together (no orphan code); the tools are single-player: 'bots collide, the merges are horrific'
relevance_to_us: 'End each step by wiring it in' guards against orphan modules; merge pain supports our interface-first split before parallel agents

who: METR (via secondary coverage, primary not fetched)
method: RCT of AI assistance on experienced devs' own repos
claim: 16 devs, 246 tasks, early-2025 tools: 19% slower with AI while believing ~20% faster
relevance_to_us: Not about design quality; a reminder that perceived pipeline effectiveness needs measuring (e.g. defects found later per design)

who: search across arXiv and practitioner posts
method: blind/independent test author vs co-written tests
claim: Found no study measuring tests written by a separate agent that never sees the implementation versus tests written alongside it. Anthropic docs endorse separating test writer and implementer; Anthropic's long-running-agents post calls specialized test agents untested
relevance_to_us: Our core differentiator is unmeasured anywhere I looked -- we could be the ones to measure it (mutation score of contract tests)
